explanation: Myth says Venus was born fully grown from the sea. Here Zephyr, the west wind, blows her ashore, while an attendant waits with a cloak embroidered with flowers.

In classical myth Venus (Aphrodite) was born fully grown from the sea.
In The Birth of Venus, Zephyr, the west wind, blows Venus ashore while an attendant waits with a cloak decorated with flowers.

evidence.restatement: Botticelli's Venus stands on a large scallop shell as she reaches the shore.
Only the shell carries her: no dolphin, lotus flower or cloud is under her feet.
In Hesiod's Theogony Aphrodite rises fully grown from the sea foam.
On the left Zephyr blows her ashore; on the right a woman, usually read as one of the Horae, holds out a cloak patterned with flowers.
